sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability. Poojaa Precision Engg. is a real, long-established aluminium casting and machining business with demonstrated organic volume expansion, not merely an IPO story. Casting output rose from 3,018 MT in FY24 to 5,049 MT in FY26, and customer concentration has gradually improved. The investment case nevertheless depends on converting a much larger capacity program into cash while cleaning up consequential reporting-control issues. FY25 lacked the statutory audit trail, the later prospectus restates profits and documents repeated bank-return differences, and IPO deployment/commitment disclosures are not yet reconciled. None of these observations establishes fraud or an actual financing default.

This is a capacity-expansion industrial growth thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder designation. At the dated secondary 19 October ₹869 reference, market capitalization is about ₹1,733 crore and FY26 restated PAT on the currently issued shares implies about 56× earnings. Even the explicitly rescue-funded base illustration earns only about 4.7% annually, far below the 15% hurdle, while a much stronger bull case works. Ordinary expected returns and buy ranges remain unscored: the model is a conditional diagnostic, not a trade recommendation. The first upgrade requires specific accounting/bank/IPO reconciliations and cash-backed operating progress, not just a lower share price.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Poojaa Precision Engg. Limited, formerly Pooja Castings Private Limited, BSE SME code 544844/PPEL, ISIN INE288301026, CIN U27310MH1992PLC068151. It listed on 4 August 2026. The economic perimeter is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards (AS), not Ind AS: the issuer reports no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures. Do not consolidate other Jayshree/promoter-group entities simply because they share relationships or operations.

Information cutoff is 20 October 2026. Historical price reference is 19 October, not a current quote; the exact ₹869 dated row agrees between IIFL and Newboard, but primary BSE bhavcopy access failed. The 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 horizon is 1,826 days divided by 365.25. The hurdle is nominal INR, pretax investor equity return of 15%; corporate tax remains modeled. ₹500,000 is only an illustrative liquidity position.

G1 is Conditional, not Fail: recurring compliance lapses, connected procurement and substantial remuneration warrant scrutiny, but disclosed pending matters are not findings of abuse. G2 is Hold: the FY25 audit-trail exception and material unreconciled bank-return history are not cured merely by a clean main opinion; FY26 improvement and published restatements are important counterevidence. G3 is Conditional: the fresh IPO and BBB+/A2 rating are positive, while actual deployment, remaining commitments and October usable cash need reconciliation. There is no verified default. G4 is Conditional: the official 400-share lot is verified, but complete 60-session traded-value/spread/restriction evidence is not.

Confidence is High in exact identity, source extraction, issued capital and disclosed restatement mechanics; Medium in organic economic growth and historical capital proxies; Low in a presently executable valuation/funding bridge and full tradeability. G2 excludes this issuer from all quality, growth-quality and investment rankings until closure, even though diagnostic quality scores are computable.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 primitive factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 3, P 2 and L NS. A scored adverse fact is different from an unknown. Revenue earns its score from observed organic expansion and volume evidence, not from planned capacity; CAP evaluates additional committed capital, not headline current ROCE; EARN concerns operating profit/per-share sources, while CASH evaluates realization.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. Contributions are 0.80, 1.00, 0.96, 0.60, 0.60, 0.30, 0.40 and 0.48, totaling 5.14, displayed 5.1. This is mixed business quality, subject to the G2 exclusion.

GQS is Growth Quality, not governance. Its REV/DUR/EARN/CAP/CASH contributions are 3.20/1.20/0.90/0.75/0.30, totaling 6.35. Persistent weak cash realization triggers the framework ceiling of 5.0; raw 6.35 and capped 5.00 are both retained. Reported three-year CFO/PAT is 0.789×, falling to 0.611× after capital-creditor reclassification and 0.485× after financing interest. Rising aged receivables reinforce the cap; growth capex alone is not the reason.

IAS uses unrounded BQS: Q contribution 1.285, D 0.600 and P 0.200. R and L are genuinely missing; their combined weight is 45%. Known contribution is 2.085 with diagnostic bounds 2.535–6.585 on a 1–10 missing-factor scale. IAS remains NS, never the midpoint or a renormalized known-factor average. All one-decimal displays use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP. GOV and CAP are the two most uncertain scored judgments: GOV determines whether adverse evidence warrants a governance override, while CAP depends on commissioning lag and capital definitions. Their ±1 sensitivities are explicitly flagged within the complete factor-sensitivity table; an adverse hypothetical GOV of 3 applies the ceiling of 3 to final BQS and IAS bounds, without asserting new adverse facts. Full factor evidence, sensitivities, gates and exact contribution rows are embedded below.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business designs and manufactures aluminium components using gravity, low-pressure and high-pressure die casting, followed by finishing, machining, assembly and testing. Melting and casting capacities describe sequential stages and must not be added as separate sales capacity. The company reports more than 600 SKUs. Commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles and EV components are important end uses, with diversification into energy, agriculture, defence and healthcare. Exports are still small; the investment case is principally Indian industrial/customer demand, not an assumed global export franchise.

Two existing Chakan/Pune units had FY26 melting capacity of 13,800 MT and casting/finishing capacity of 6,000 MT. Actual production of 10,982 MT melting and 5,049 MT casting means roughly 80%/84% utilization. The Unit III plan adds 15,000 MT melting and 6,600 MT casting, taking combined nameplate casting to 12,600 MT. Unit III is leased; only part of the available factory area forms the initial project. The expansion therefore requires customer approvals, machines, people, yields and sustained orders, not simply floor space.

Revenue reflects metal pass-through as well as component value added, precision and product mix. Aluminium accounted for ₹99.4304 crore, or 72.43% of FY26 raw-material cost. The issuer seeks to pass metal cost increases to customers, but describes timing gaps and customer pricing pressure. Accordingly, revenue per ton is only a mix/realization diagnostic. Operating economics should be followed through casting output, contribution/EBIT, scrap/yields, receivable collection and full capital committed, rather than assuming metal-price inflation is demand growth.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable capabilities. Three decades of casting/process know-how, customer qualification, tooling and integrated machining can make switching costly and create recurring business. Yet the evidence does not establish irreplaceable technology, exclusive contracts, dominant market share or unconstrained pricing. Customers can cancel purchase orders, do not promise take-or-pay volumes, and can impose pricing pressure. A high reported margin is therefore not by itself a durable moat.

Concentration remains material: FY26 top customer was 31.75%, top two about 50.55%, top five 74.72% and top ten 88.64%. The reduction from 84.42% top-five concentration in FY24 is real counterevidence against a deteriorating customer mix, but still leaves operating leverage exposed to a small set of buyers. Related-party material and job-work supply is useful capacity support but should be checked against external pricing and alternative suppliers.

The prospectus compares Alicon Castalloy, Rico Auto and Endurance Technologies. They are useful process/customer-context peers, not interchangeable valuation twins: sizes, products, export mixes and capital intensity differ. Its June 30 peer P/E snapshot is historical and is not compared mechanically with an October Poojaa quote. The report gives no extra moat points for SME status, a prominent customer logo, an oversubscribed IPO or a strong early stock-price performance.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The consistent IPO-restated series is revenue ₹163.3792/173.7222/221.9993/293.8554 crore in FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26. Three-year CAGR is 21.61%; annual growth accelerated from 6.33% to 27.79% and 32.37%. Legacy signed FY21/FY22 revenue of ₹87.1147/130.0896 crore gives a five-year FY21–26 reported CAGR of 27.53%. That older window is shown, not hidden, but the selected economic scoring window is the consistent FY23–26 restated series because the COVID-era base and legacy accounting classifications are less representative. Both windows fall in the same REV starting band of 8, so the choice does not manufacture an upgrade.

No subsidiary or acquired operation was identified in the disclosed period. Casting output rose at 29.34% CAGR from FY24 to FY26; melting output rose 34.89%. FY26 casting volume growth was about 50.6%, exceeding revenue growth, while revenue per casting ton fell about 12.1%. This supports genuine physical scaling and cautions against treating total rupee growth as pure pricing power. Output mix, gross/net metal content and sequential melting yields still prevent a precise homogeneous volume/price decomposition.

REV remains 8 with no trajectory bonus. The older H1 FY26 restated numbers, ₹124.888 crore revenue and ₹10.2581 crore PAT, are not a newer FY27 update. FY27 half-year results became available on 22 October and are excluded from this 20 October decision set. No current-quarter growth, order book or customer award is invented. The important next confirmation is sustained revenue and cash conversion after commissioning, not extrapolation from one launch announcement.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
DUR 6 recognizes accessible demand from lightweight aluminium components, non-auto diversification and existing customer access, while acknowledging automotive cyclicality, concentrated customers and a large ramp. Unit III can more than double nameplate casting capacity, but capacity is not contracted demand. The solar installation is included inside the ₹110.4308 crore project; it is not an additional free profit source or a separate capex charge. The proposed magnesium direction is a possible future avenue, not a funded, order-backed base-case business.

CAP 5 uses the same-issuer multi-year capital bridge, not the prospectus’s 26.38% current ROCE alone. Committed-capital proxy rises from ₹61.6291 crore in March 2023 to ₹186.8019 crore in March 2026. Normalized NOPAT at 25.17% tax rises from ₹15.1623 crore to ₹34.0265 crore. Incremental return is therefore about 15.07% on ₹125.1728 crore additional capital, around a reasoned nominal INR post-tax cost-of-capital range of 12–16%, not clearly exceptional. Excluding CWIP and capital advances gives a commissioned-capital proxy around 19.42%; the FY23–25 earlier window is about 23.98%. Those are useful lag/commissioning views, not proof the new factory earns that return.

The capital proxy includes restricted operating margins, security deposits, CWIP, capital advances and supplier-funded capital creditors; financial investments and intercorporate loans are excluded. ₹86.1923 crore cumulative presented capex minus ₹16.5775 crore depreciation plus ₹54.0349 crore ONWC increase explains ₹123.6497 crore capital growth, with a ₹1.5231 crore reconciled residual: ₹2.0289 crore other noncurrent operating-asset increase less ₹0.5058 crore net fixed-asset/disposal/restatement residual. The remaining fixed-asset residual is explicitly unresolved at transaction level rather than silently attributed to project returns. Five-year incremental ROIC is NS because older legacy capital classifications have not been reconciled to the IPO-restated perimeter.

Growth quality is further constrained by operating realization. The capped GQS of 5.0 is not a claim that demand disappears; it recognizes that rapid growth financed through inventory, overdue buyers and delayed supplier payment is less valuable than the same growth paid in cash. Full project cash, recurring maintenance and post-IPO growth investment remain in every valuation scenario.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
GOV 4 reflects specific stewardship concerns, not guilt by association. The prospectus discloses repeated failures to place declared dividends in a separate bank account within the required period, earlier company-secretary compliance issues, delayed ROC filings and charge-registration issues. It describes adjudication/compounding applications and remediation. Historical director disqualifications and pending proceedings involving promoter-group interests are disclosed; none is treated here as a proven fraud, conviction or a current disqualification without evidence.

FY26 related-party goods purchases were ₹30.5321 crore, job-work/services ₹4.8055 crore, promoter professional services ₹1.44 crore, and disclosed KMP short-term benefits about ₹9.1955 crore. Procurement and remuneration are costs already included in profitability, not automatic add-backs. The issuer states transactions are ordinary-course and arm’s length, but independent bid/pricing comparisons are not supplied. Future ₹50 crore transaction ceilings for each of two related suppliers are approval limits, not amounts already spent. Promoter ownership is about 60.63% post-IPO; it aligns exposure but cannot replace minority safeguards. The IPO is fresh issuance rather than an OFS cash-out.

EXEC 6 balances tangible delivered output expansion against the next project’s larger scale. Casting output and utilization increased before the IPO; that is a meaningful operating record. The planned remaining project spend runs to June 2027. Secondary announcement leads refer to Unit III and solar commencement, but without the full primary filings and production/collection proof they are not treated as validation that every budgeted machine is operating at designed utilization. The 17 September investor-meeting document is only an intimation, not a presentation or management forecast.

FY26 audit-trail operation and the detailed IPO restatement are positive steps. They do not automatically close missing FY25 logs or explain why older clean bank-return descriptions differ from the later disclosure. A dated, specific remediation package would improve governance confidence far more than generic assurances.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Use the latest comparable restated series, not a mixture of annual statutory PAT and offer-document cash flows. FY26 statutory PAT ₹33.4518 crore is reduced by ₹2.5490 crore to ₹30.9028 crore. FY25 is increased by ₹1.4926 crore to ₹23.9308 crore; FY24 reduces ₹0.0560 crore to ₹16.0965 crore. FY26 adjustments include obsolete-die inventory −₹3.2678 crore, gratuity −₹0.2428 crore, depreciation −₹0.1264 crore, leasehold write-off reversal +₹0.6872 crore, and related tax/expense/FX corrections. The entire bridge is retained. These are disclosed corrections, but material corrections weaken the claim of effortless earnings quality.

FY26 PBT ₹42.4637 crore plus all finance cost ₹4.3520 crore less all other income ₹1.3439 crore gives EBIT ₹45.4718 crore; adding depreciation ₹6.5200 gives EBITDA ₹51.9918 crore. The offer’s EBITDA ₹51.7765 uses interest rather than all finance costs, a ₹0.2153 crore borrowing-fee definition difference, not a new financial error. A conservative EBIT that retains statutory/MSME interest is ₹45.0533 crore. No obsolete inventory, wages, related procurement, CSR or lease rent is automatically normalized away. Other income is small but is stripped out consistently; it is not valued as repeatable operating profit.

The published FY24–26 CFO/PAT total is ₹55.9398/70.9301 crore, 0.789×. FY26 CFO ₹23.7980 crore includes ₹12.5842 crore capital-creditor growth in other liabilities. Removing that financing benefit yields ₹11.2138 crore operating CFO and reduces presented capex by the same amount, preserving free cash flow. Three-year adjusted CFO is ₹43.3556 crore, 0.611× PAT, and after cash financing interest only 0.485×. Three-year FCF is negative ₹30.2525 crore before interest and negative ₹39.1865 crore after interest. Expansion accounts for much of investment, but not for worsening receivable quality.

Receivables plus unbilled revenue move from 39.8 revenue-days in FY23 to 69.2 days FY26. Gross receivables older than six months rise from ₹2.0833 crore FY25 to ₹7.0414 crore FY26; over-one-year gross is ₹3.6939 crore and allowance ₹0.4766 crore. Unbilled revenue rises from ₹0.6554 to ₹3.8943 crore. Inventory grows from ₹27.0580 to ₹50.6967 crore. These balances are not declared uncollectible, but collections, obsolete dies and rate adjustments require evidence.

Full audit review matters. FY25’s signed Rule 11(g) says the accounting software lacked edit logs and logs were not preserved; FY26 says logs operated, were not tampered with and were preserved. Main opinions and IFC are unmodified, but that is not an all-clear on annexures. The IPO statements list quarterly bank-return differences throughout FY24–26. Management cites finalization timing, advances/TDS and supplementary price provisions. In FY26 Q4 bank inventory and receivable figures exceed books by ₹3.9673 and ₹4.6470 crore, while Q1 books receivables exceed returns by ₹12.4192 crore. Published and arithmetic difference columns preserve ₹0.01-lakh rounding discrepancies. Bank acknowledgment/closure has not been retrieved.

Cash is not ₹4.9031 crore freely available: only ₹0.3674 crore was unrestricted at March 2026, with ₹4.5357 crore in margin deposits. ₹2.4288 crore intercorporate loans and ₹0.1200 crore investments are not assumed immediately spendable. Debt rises from ₹41.1587 crore March to ₹70.8256 crore June. Full IPO proceeds are separately recognized; the BBB+/A2 rating and successful raise counter a simplistic insolvency narrative. Yet the annual board’s “fully utilized” wording conflicts with its proposed allocation table and prospectus phasing, and ₹82.0469 crore annual capital commitments differ from ₹10.1748 crore prospectus commitments. Scope or drafting may explain this, but no reconciliation is invented. G2 remains Hold and G3 Conditional.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated ₹869 quote and 19,944,960 currently issued shares imply about ₹1,733.22 crore equity value. FY26 restated PAT divided by these shares gives approximately ₹15.49 EPS and 56.09× P/E. Using the pre-IPO weighted-average ₹21.90 EPS would produce a misleadingly lower multiple because it ignores the fresh share issuance. IPO ₹301 is neither intrinsic value nor a support level. Unissued ESOPs are not part of current market capitalization; the model separately tests all 146,350 shares with zero exercise proceeds.

EV/EBIT is the primary framework for this lease-expensed manufacturer. EBIT includes rent; no duplicate lease liability or operating-property value is added. Reported margins and an industrial-peer context inform, but do not prove, 12×/18×/24× terminal EBIT assumptions in bear/base/bull. The final trailing-12-month earnings end exactly 20 October 2031, not an entire future FY32. Terminal cash retains an operating reserve, restricted margins and remaining earmarks are not added as distributable surplus, and recurring investment persists after the IPO capex budget ends.

The model starts July 2026 so that pre-IPO funding cannot be hidden. June debt ₹70.8256 crore is disclosed; June unrestricted cash ₹3 crore and operating WC ₹82 crore are explicit assumptions. IPO cash timing is conservatively placed on 4 August, the verified listing/raise date, not asserted as a verified bank-credit date. ₹139.9121 crore net proceeds split into ₹106.3359 crore eligible project/bridge money, ₹30 crore WC and ₹3.5762 crore GCP. The already-spent ₹18.7492 crore bridge is repaid once; future project cash is ₹87.5867 crore. The ₹0.3154 crore prepaid IPO charge is recouped once, old tax/statutory/interest balances settle separately, and capital-creditor overlap is stressed at 0/50/100% rather than double counted. No uncommitted credit line is treated as cash.

With ₹3 crore opening cash and a ₹2 crore required reserve, all headline non-rescue scenarios breach a pre-entry cash floor under conservative payment-before-inflow timing. Their returns and hurdle entry prices are therefore null. This is not observed distress. Explicit whole-share pre-funded rescue variants repair the interval trough and show dilution/fees separately. The rescued base produces roughly 4.7% annualized price return, bear about −20.8%, bull about 20.6%; no probabilities are assigned. Raising assumed opening cash to ₹8 crore can make the base internally funded, but leaves ordinary returns NS because actual cash/deployment and reliability remain unverified.

Reverse expectations recompute funding and dilution and verify a finite bracket/residual. At 18× terminal EBIT, a 15% hurdle requires roughly 28.8% annual revenue growth under a sustained 16% terminal EBIT margin, compared with the 21.6% historical three-year revenue CAGR; at 12× it requires about 39.5%, at 24× about 22.2%. These are conditional funded solutions, not attainable guidance. Two-way WC/project-cost, opening-cash/reserve, growth/multiple and creditor-overlap/interest grids plus 12/15/18% hurdles show where financing or valuation breaks. P 2 reflects the optimistic conjunction required at this price; R remains NS, not the rescue illustration mechanically scored.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest credible bear case starts with demand and collection, not an unsupported accusation. A major automotive customer cuts orders or delays lifting goods; new casting capacity is underutilized; fixed costs and higher factory rent reduce margin; inventory and rate-adjustment receivables absorb cash; bridge/debt service and installation obligations still fall due. Related suppliers and banks then determine how much flexibility remains. The stock can suffer permanent impairment from issuing equity on weak terms or from normalization of a high entry multiple even if the company survives.

The bear model links low growth, a 10–11% EBIT margin, WC at 38% of sales, project overrun of 15%, ongoing maintenance and growth capex, and a 12× exit EBIT multiple. Its no-rescue cash path is infeasible and has no valid return. The explicit rescue path requires material new funding, pays fees and dilutes existing ownership; its approximate negative 21% annualized shareholder result is a conditional impairment illustration, not a probability or a forecast of actual distress. The actual IPO raise, healthy recent interest cover and Crisil’s adequate liquidity view are important contrary evidence and prevent a default classification.

The central falsifier is whether incremental production converts into reliable collected earnings after the full expansion capital is committed. Additional quarterly sales alone do not falsify this bear case if receivables, inventory and supplier-financed capex rise faster. Conversely, verified bank reconciliations, audit-trail remediation, contracted customer ramps and two reporting periods of strong adjusted cash conversion would materially weaken it. A stock-price fall without new operating evidence is neither proof of misconduct nor proof of a bargain.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold stock price in this exact five-year horizon requires about 38.0% annual price growth; tenfold requires about 58.5%. That is not equivalent to a fivefold/tentfold revenue objective. The decomposition must include net margins, terminal P/E and additional shares. The current roughly 56× FY26 current-capital P/E already capitalizes a large growth expectation.

The embedded feasibility rows assume a 10.5% terminal net margin and all currently authorized ESOP shares, without additional rescue dilution, and test lower terminal P/Es of 15× and 25×. Required equity, PAT, revenue, revenue growth and indicative casting tonnage are calculated explicitly. They imply revenue several times the planned 12,600-MT capacity’s output at FY26 mix/realization. More capacity, capital, working capital, customer diversification and potentially additional shares would be required; none is assumed to arrive free of charge. At a 25× terminal P/E the 5× price outcome alone needs around ₹3,326 crore revenue, versus ₹293.9 crore FY26, before any extra financing dilution.

The available order/customer evidence does not support that accessible market share or funded scale. Both outcomes are classified Speculative / unsupported, not impossible. The appropriate question is whether cash-backed returns on the already committed expansion can beat the cost of capital; a distant multibagger story cannot override the current reliability Hold.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor reporting events, not stock-price targets. The following thresholds are research alerts grounded in the current economics, not automatic buy/sell rules, and no recurring automation is created.

1. Bank-return reconciliation: baseline differences across FY24–26; obtain a period-by-period reconciliation, eligibility/advance/netting definitions and bank/auditor acknowledgment. New unexplained differences or contradictory lender evidence is a thesis-break alert. Review with the next financial release.
2. Audit trail and restatement: FY25 logs absent; FY26 claims operating/preserved. Confirm scope and sustained remediation with the next statutory report and obtain closure of material inventory/gratuity/depreciation corrections. Another material unbridged restatement escalates G2.
3. IPO deployment: ₹139.9121 crore net, ₹106.3359 project/bridge, ₹30 WC. Reconcile bank balance, object-wise spend, ₹18.7492 bridge repayment and unpaid capex; explain the fully-utilized wording and commitment discrepancy. Diversion or unauthorized objects would be a distinct governance escalation, not assumed today.
4. Capacity and collection: initial casting 5,049 MT versus 6,000 MT installed; planned 12,600 MT total. Check commissioning, yields, sustained customer demand and collection. Delays beyond June 2027 without a funded revised plan or persistently idle equipment weaken DUR/EXEC/CAP.
5. Cash realization: FY24–26 adjusted CFO/PAT 0.611×. Improvement toward at least 0.8× across two periods would be constructive; another period below 0.6× with growing overdue balances demands investigation. Exclude capital-creditor increases and financing interest consistently.
6. Working capital: gross receivables >6 months ₹7.0414 crore, unbilled ₹3.8943 crore and inventory ₹50.6967 crore. Growth faster than sales, new disputes or further obsolete-die write-offs merit a tighter cash stress. Collections with no factoring/debt substitution are the favorable test.
7. Concentration and related parties: top five 74.72%, top customer 31.75%. Track customer loss, actual procurement against approved ceilings and independent price benchmarking. A larger approval ceiling alone is not a breach.
8. Funding: June debt ₹70.8256 crore; rating BBB+/Stable/A2 and IPO are supportive. Watch net usable cash, principal schedule, lease rent and covenant/credit-line status; a verified default is different from an analyst reserve breach.
9. Market implementation: verify exact new lot effective 16 November, live spread/circuits/surveillance and a complete recent traded-value sample. Recalculate whole-lot capacity for an actual position before implementation; current ₹5 lakh reference is not a suitable-size recommendation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved financial reliability, with a mixed-quality industrial expansion business beneath it. BQS 5.14 (5.1 display), raw GQS 6.35 capped at 5.00, and IAS NS are diagnostic assessments only. This is not an evidence-backed compounder, not a proven fraud and not a verified funding failure. All ranking eligibility flags are false because G2 is material; missing R/L independently prevent a complete IAS.

Research priority is resolution of the specific controls, banking and IPO-use questions, not an executable buy range. A lower price can improve arithmetic without resolving G2. Conversely, a credible reconciliation can remove a gate without making a 56× trailing setup attractive. Re-run the economic model with verified cash/debt/earmarks and updated customer/collection evidence before scoring R or publishing an ordinary entry price.

For an existing holder, this is a thesis/reliability/valuation review candidate, not an instruction to exit a specified number of shares. Actual weights, liquidity, taxes and investor objectives have not been supplied. No security trade or external communication is authorized by this research. The report should remain in the SME research group, using the same methodology and complete format as main-board work without conflating the two universes.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes the full final 31 July prospectus, full July RHP, March draft with FY23 accounts, FY26 annual report, signed FY21–FY25 accounts and complete relevant audit annexures, and the July/August Crisil publications. Source URLs and payload SHA-256 hashes, exact fact locators, status/confidence and contrary evidence are retained. The official dated interoperability security master verifies ISIN/capital/lot, while dated secondary histories supply the price and partial turnover sample. Secondary IPO summaries and rolling prices do not substitute for the full filed accounts. The September investor-meeting notice supplies no earnings guidance.

The canonical financial rows retain legacy versus restated basis, unadjusted versus analytically reclassified cash flows, all restatement/bank-difference rows, annual operating forecasts, every dated funding row, all sensitivity/reverse/5×–10× rows, gate decisions and factor calculations. Safe rebuild inputs contain extracted financial facts and provenance, not original shareholder lists or personal identifiers. Reproduction can verify calculations from retained facts; it does not newly authenticate an unavailable exchange document.

Unresolved questions are precise: why did older CARO bank-return descriptions differ from later restatement tables; can FY25 logging shortcomings be remediated and reconciled; what is the actual post-IPO unrestricted versus earmarked cash/debt bridge; how do ₹82.0469 crore annual and ₹10.1748 crore prospectus capital commitments reconcile; which capital creditors are already inside project spend; what are current customer commitments, overdue collections and expansion yields; and what are current spreads/restrictions? Old tax and other obligations, potential prepayment charges, ungranted ESOPs and lease costs remain explicit model assumptions.

The cutoff excludes FY27 half-year results released 22 October, later price rows and the future-effective 200-share lot. The analysis is research, not a forecast guarantee, personalized portfolio allocation or instruction to transact. Subsequent evidence should update the same assumptions and gates rather than backfill hindsight into this dated assessment.

interpretation: All capex, WC, recurring growth investment, debt principal, interest, taxes and lease-inclusive margins extend only to 20 October 2031. No post-terminal cash flows or future free residual IPO money are added.

Operating leases remain fully in EBIT/cash economics. No extra lease-debt subtraction or duplicate operating-property valuation; no NCI or acquisitions. Rent increase after new factory must fit scenario margins.

Old liabilities are settled once and excluded from model opening operating WC. Capital-creditor baseline is inside project budget, with 0/50/100% overlap sensitivity. Prepaid IPO costs are recouped once; full fees are not charged twice.

No dividends are assumed; retained cash accumulates after required reinvestment. Restricted deposits remain unavailable and terminal reserve is preserved. No uncommitted bank line is automatically drawn.

A modeled reserve breach is an analyst assumption outcome, not evidence of actual distress. Non-rescue return and entry values are null after any pre-entry or later breach. Rescue explicitly issues whole shares before uses and pays issuance fees.
Terminal ESOP pool is conservatively fully exercised without proceeds, although grants and exercise price are unconfirmed; ordinary current capitalization remains issued shares only.

summary:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability. Poojaa Precision Engg. is a real, long-established aluminium casting and machining business with demonstrated organic volume expansion, not merely an IPO story. Casting output rose from 3,018 MT in FY24 to 5,049 MT in FY26, and customer concentration has gradually improved. The investment case nevertheless depends on converting a much larger capacity program into cash while cleaning up consequential reporting-control issues. FY25 lacked the statutory audit trail, the later prospectus restates profits and documents repeated bank-return differences, and IPO deployment/commitment disclosures are not yet reconciled. None of these observations establishes fraud or an actual financing default.

This is a capacity-expansion industrial growth thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder designation. At the dated secondary 19 October ₹869 reference, market capitalization is about ₹1,733 crore and FY26 restated PAT on the currently issued shares implies about 56× earnings. Even the explicitly rescue-funded base illustration earns only about 4.7% annually, far below the 15% hurdle, while a much stronger bull case works. Ordinary expected returns and buy ranges remain unscored: the model is a conditional diagnostic, not a trade recommendation. The first upgrade requires specific accounting/bank/IPO reconciliations and cash-backed operating progress, not just a lower share price.
